steps.text: Combine ground beef with 1/2 of the minced garlic and 1 tablespoon chopped onion in a large bowl. Mix with your hands until fully incorporated. Shape meat mixture into 1 1/2-inch oblong patties; you should have 12 to 14 meatballs.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown patties in batches in the hot skillet until crispy on both sides and no longer pink in the center, about 10 minutes. Set meatballs aside in a rimmed serving dish.

Reduce heat to medium and stir remaining chopped onion into drippings in the skillet. Season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in remaining garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in Roma tomatoes, dried parsley, and ras el hanout. Pour in water. Cook until tomatoes are soft, about 5 minutes.
Pour tomato sauce over meatballs to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Algerian Kefta (Meatballs)
raw_recipe.description: These simple ground beef meatballs in a garlicky fresh Roma tomato sauce are best served with a crusty French baguette.

review.reviewBody: These meatballs put inside a French baguette make a pretty good meatball sandwich. However, I think I would throw a little ras el handout into the ground beef if I made it again to give the meat a little more flavor.

Delicious. Followed the directions except that I took the advice of another, and added the Ras el hanout to the meat as well. Delicate and distinct flavors make this dish a simple, clean, culinary delight. My children are not necessarily picky eaters, but spice can be challenging to a child’s palate and this dish won them over. I doubled up on the recipe, and it fed a hungry family of 4 with leftovers for a single lunch (in other words- it was devoured!). Beautiful recipe and very simple to make. Thank you for sharing your wonderful family dish and I will be adding this recipe as a staple menu item. Also, I made the ras el hanout. Very easy to make and requires readily available spices. I give this recipe 5 stars all around- looks nice, smells wonderful, tastes amazing, takes under an hour from start to finish (even with making the spice), but most of all- will be enjoyed by all sorts of eaters- from finicky to those that will eat anything.

This recipe was absolutely fabulous! As a Caribbean girl, getting a North African spice blend during COVID was out of the question, so I researched and made my own blend of ras el hanout from 16 ground spices that I had on hand. The meatballs were made from equal amounts of minced lamb and beef, seasoned with chopped garlic and onions along with a generous sprinkling of my homemade ras el hanout blend. Had no plum tomatoes, so I substituted tomato sauce after deglazing the au jus. Another generous dash of ras el hanout and a sprinkle of brown sugar (I seldom use measurements when cooking) absolutely transformed the taste of the tomato sauce. The meatballs and the thick, tasty sauce which developed were served and sopped up with some freshly baked bread. I think I'm in looooove!! With all my changes, this recipe may no longer be authentically Algerian, but it certainly was tasty!! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

I've made kefta once before with beef. It was plain and dry. I decided to try this with ground chicken. I baked in it the oven, with some panko and olive oil added (because the chicken was astonishingly well ground, like a paste). I read some of the other reviews and put some Ras el Hanout in. Stuck to the recipe otherwise. All in all, quite good and nicely browned. Regarding the Ras el Hanout, I cut the cinnamon as others suggested. I also added 5 Spice Powder and cardamom. Since the 5 Spices include cloves, I'd recommend on cutting the other cloves back too.

The flavor of the sauce was wonderful but I will, in the future, par boil the tomatoes first to remove the skin or just use canned diced tomatoes. Just a personal preference to not have the separated skin floating around. I agree the meat needed seasoning as well, so I’ll try that next time.

Smash hit @ the meatball potluck.

I added a 1/2 tsp of the spice mix and a 1/2 tsp of dried parsley to the meat directly to tie the flavors together.

I will make it again.

Next time I am going to try searing the meatballs on high heat then bringing them to full temp in the sauce. The meatballs were a touch dry and I had trouble getting them over 140 degrees internally without risking burning the outsides.

Very delicious and classic dish! The added water is entirely unnecessary- makes the sauce very diluted and runny. Instead of using a pre-made set of ras el hanout, I make my own mix of cumin, coriander, ginger, salt, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, cayenne, and paprika. That being said, since even pre-made blends have salt and pepper in them already, be careful to not over-salt!

Next time I will be also adding some mint leaves with the onion, to add a little Moroccan kick.

Excellent, simple recipe. Please don't avoid the optional spice, which can be obtained through Amazon if you don't live near a store that carries it in a more rural area. It adds a touch of sweetness and aroma- I also used Amish paste tomatoes as opposed to the Roma, because I prefer their slightly sweeter taste- these are harder to find, depending on where you live, but it's another take on this great recipe! We also preferred rice with ours but the bread sounds like a wonderful idea...

Wonderful dinner! I served it over rice and substituted a few pinches of cumin and lemon zest for the ras el hanout, and fresh parsley for dried. Also left out the water as the tomatoes made it saucy enough and made the meatballs a bit more bite-sized. Otherwise, terrific!

I loved these. I made them exactly as called for - but used minced onion instead of chopped. For the tomato sauce - I got creative and added: 1 can rotel, 1 can of italian stewed tomatoes, sofrito (from the spanish isle), some salsa, splash of A1 bold, a 1/2 lime (squeezed), more sofrito, pepper and some cumin. Sofrito adds a little zip and spice to the sauce, as I did not have ras el hanout. Simmer on low and added on top of the meatballs. It was SO good and my company for dinner that night were AMAZED! This is my new "go to" recipe for meatballs. My FAVE!

4 stars only because I did make a few changes. I used the link provided in the notes for the ras el hanout (I did cut back on the cinnamon) and put a teaspoon into the meat mixture, and doubled the amount in the tomato mixture. These meatballs were excellent; I served them with homemade pita breads and tomato/cucumber/feta salad. Very different and very yummy! Thanks for the inspiration!
I made it with ground turkey and added smoked paprika and added Raz el hanout to the mix. I also added some red wine to the sauce. Very good!

I stretched this out to 4 servings. The sauce was flavorful, so I will double that the next time. Will use the ras el hanout or other herbs in addition to the onion and garlic the next time! Made this on a week night. Easy! Thanks for the recipe.

I'm eating this right now and it isn't good enough for me to want to make it again, even with mods. I like the flavor of the ras el hanout. I also like the sauce -- the fresh tomatoes are the hero there. However, overall the dish needs more flavor even though I added an additional half teaspoon of ras el hanout to the meatballs and used 2-3 pinches of salt in the sauce and 1-2 pinches in the meatballs. Sadly, my wife feels just the opposite, saying that the spices in the dish overwhelmed her tastebuds so that she now can't really taste the flavors of the fresh tomato or onion. To me, the garlic is overpowering, so I would recommend cutting that by 1/4. I would also double or triple the amount of onions added to the sauce. But when it seems a dish would require a lot of experimentation and guesswork (and failures) to earn a place on my "make this again" list, it's just not worth my time. We'll finish this dish, but won't make it again.
Loved it. I added a little too much water with the tomatoes, but other than that it was delicious

Made this exactly as it listed, except added a bit more garlic and onion to the ground beef as well as ras el hanout to give the meat a bit more flavor. It turned out fantastic! One of the best dishes I’ve tried in a while and will definitely make it again.
All good

DEFINITELY USE RAS EL HANOUT, gives it a wonderful flavor! Would be bland otherwise! Overall I give it 4 stars.. I would like to add a little more flavorings to the meat. I followed it to the T and it came out good, next time will season the beef a little more before cooking.
Delicious! Love flavorful food. Only thing I changed was mix in some of the Ras El Hanout and tiny bit more salt into the meat to enhance the flavors throughout. Thanks for sharing!
really good. I did tweak it somewhat, adding another measure of ras el hanout in with the meat, and using canned diced tomatoes (it's not tomato season yet)
